title: The Role of Microplastics in Marine Ecosystems

sections.heading: Reading Passage 1
sections.passage: Microplastics, tiny plastic particles less than five millimeters in size, have become a pervasive environmental pollutant in recent decades. They enter marine ecosystems through various pathways, such as wastewater treatment plants, stormwater runoff, and even atmospheric deposition. Once in the ocean, microplastics can have significant ecological effects, posing threats to marine life ranging from plankton to large marine mammals. These particles can be ingested by marine organisms, leading to physical and chemical harm. For instance, studies have shown that microplastics can cause inflammation and other health issues in fish, which can have cascading effects on the food web. Furthermore, microplastics can act as vectors for toxic substances, accumulating harmful chemicals from the surrounding water and transporting them through the food chain. The prevalence of microplastics has raised concerns among scientists regarding their potential impact on marine biodiversity and ecosystems. Some researchers suggest that the accumulation of these particles could alter habitat structures and affect species diversity. Efforts to mitigate microplastic pollution include improving waste management practices, banning certain types of plastic products, and raising public awareness about the issue. Although steps are being taken to address the problem, many experts believe that comprehensive regulations are necessary to significantly reduce microplastic pollution and its effects on marine life.

questions.question: Microplastics enter marine ecosystems only through wastewater treatment plants.
questions.explanation: The passage states that microplastics enter through various pathways, not exclusively through wastewater treatment plants.

questions.question: What is one potential effect of microplastics on marine life?
options: B) They cause inflammation in fish
questions.explanation: The passage explicitly states that microplastics can cause inflammation and other health issues in fish.

questions.question: Complete the sentence. Choose no more than two words.

questions.question: What is the size range of microplastics?

questions.question: Many experts believe that __________ regulations are necessary to reduce microplastic pollution significantly.
questions.prompt: Complete the sentence. Choose no more than two words.
questions.explanation: The passage states that many experts believe comprehensive regulations are necessary to reduce pollution.

questions.question: Which type of marine life is mentioned as being affected by microplastics?
